citations.narrative:
In the outdoor portion of the primary enclosure that houses 3 adult mini–Australian Shepherds there is a wood board
along the bottom section of the building wall in disrepair. An approximately 4 X 2-inch hole is present in the wood board
with jagged edges that the dogs can contact. The dogs are also able to contact the metal planks that run along the
outdoor portion of the primary enclosure, which are in disrepair with multiple pinpoint size areas of red to orange rust and
corrosion. The jagged edges of the hole in the wood board and the corroded and rusty areas of the metal create a hazard.
Housing facilities for dogs must be designed and constructed so that they are structurally sound. They must be kept in
good repair, and they must protect the animals from injury.
Correct by: September 21, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
Robert Ferguson, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
